step_by_step_instructions.title: Establish the True Architectural Centroid (Nābhi / Brahma-sthāna)
step_by_step_instructions.instruction: Locate the geometric center of your dwelling's floor plate. For rectangular or square plans, draw intersecting diagonals from opposite outer corners. For articulated or irregular layouts, determine the center of mass.
step_by_step_instructions.erudite_tip: The central 1/9th area represents the Brahma-sthāna—the luminous cosmic core that must remain free of heavy structural columns or septic penetrations.

step_by_step_instructions.title: Determine Precise Cardinal Orientation (Dig-Māna)

step_by_step_instructions.erudite_tip: A deviation exceeding 15 degrees shifts the spatial diagnostic from a cardinal grid (Dik-Sādhana) to a diagonal matrix (Kona-Sādhana), altering the padavinyāsa calculations.

step_by_step_instructions.title: Map Functional Zones to the 81-Pada Grid
step_by_step_instructions.instruction: Superimpose the 9x9 Paramaśāyika Maṇḍala over your architectural plan. Assign each primary functional space—entrance, kitchen, master retreat, puja sanctuary, washrooms, and staircases—to its respective quadrant.
step_by_step_instructions.erudite_tip: Notice how the diagonal axis running from Northeast (Īśāna) to Southwest (Nairṛtya) governs the prāṇic gradient: weight must taper in the Northeast and concentrate in the Southwest.

methodology_explainer.cosmic_geometry: The Vāstu Puruṣa Maṇḍala forms the transcendental blueprint for human habitation. The Paramaśāyika configuration partitions the spatial envelope into 9x9 = 81 squares, governed by 45 divine energies (32 outer peripheral devatās and 13 inner deities). The cosmic puruṣa lies recumbent with head oriented toward the Northeast (Īśāna) and feet anchored in the Southwest (Nairṛtya).
methodology_explainer.elemental_dynamics_panchabhuta: The five elements govern distinct spatial octants: Water (Jala) in the Northeast, Fire (Agni) in the Southeast, Earth (Pṛthvī) in the Southwest, Air (Vāyu) in the Northwest, and Space (Ākāśa) vibrating freely in the central Brahma-sthāna. Domestic harmony is achieved when structural functions mirror the innate thermodynamic and psychological properties of these elements.
methodology_explainer.solar_and_magnetic_science: Classical Vastu synthesizes two profound natural forces: Prāṇic energy, flowing with early solar ultraviolet radiation from the East, and Jaiva energy, governed by Earth's geomagnetic flux running South to North. Shelters designed with open, low, and permeable northern and eastern boundaries maximize vital biological vitality.
methodology_explainer.marma_points: The intersection of diagonal diagonal lines (Karṇa-sūtras) and grid boundaries forms vulnerable nodes called Marmas. The central navel, heart, and cranial crossings must remain unobstructed by load-bearing masonry to ensure spatial respiration.

step_by_step_instructions.title: Survey Site Geometry & Aspect Ratios (Ākāra-Vicāra)
step_by_step_instructions.instruction: Measure the precise boundary dimensions across all four perimeter edges and diagonal distances. Check whether the site forms a true square (Caturaśra) or a harmonic rectangle (Āyata) with an aspect ratio not exceeding 1:2.
step_by_step_instructions.erudite_tip: Unequal diagonal chords create Karṇa-Doṣa (diagonal torsion), generating subconscious tension among occupants unless energetically rectified.

step_by_step_instructions.title: Chart Topographical Slope & Water Runoff (Jala-Plāvana)
step_by_step_instructions.instruction: Determine the natural gravitational slope of the land using a topographical survey or spirit level. Confirm whether surface runoff flows naturally toward the North, East, or Northeast.
step_by_step_instructions.erudite_tip: The classical texts describe 'Gaja-Pṛṣṭha' (Elephant back—high in the center and south) as auspicious, and 'Kūrma-Pṛṣṭha' (Tortoise back—elevated center) as bestower of wealth.

step_by_step_instructions.title: Conduct the Classical Soil Vitality Tests (Mṛttikā-Parīkṣā)
step_by_step_instructions.instruction: Perform the ancient pit-water absorption test (Garta-Parīkṣā): dig a 1-cubit (18x18 inch) pit at sunset, fill it with water, and inspect the residual water level after 100 paces or overnight.
step_by_step_instructions.erudite_tip: Soil that retains water overnight is classified as 'Pradakṣiṇā-Snigdha'—endowed with fertile subterranean moisture and high cohesive energy.

step_by_step_instructions.title: Audit Surrounding Roads & Environmental Vectors (Vīthi-Vedha)
step_by_step_instructions.instruction: Examine intersecting roads, T-junctions, and dead-ends terminating directly at the property boundaries. Identify any high-velocity vehicular vectors hitting the site.
step_by_step_instructions.erudite_tip: Road vectors arriving from the Northeast are prāṇic enhancers, whereas those striking the Southwest require deflection barriers to prevent kinetic turbulence.

methodology_explainer.cosmic_geometry: Classical site diagnostics begin with the macro-envelope. The earth absorbs cosmic vibrations along its magnetic and solar meridians. Square (Caturaśra) and proportional rectangular (Āyata) plots establish a stable four-pillar foundation where the peripheral 32 devatās find uninterrupted sanctuary.
methodology_explainer.elemental_dynamics_panchabhuta: The site's topography establishes the elemental hierarchy: the Southwest represents Earth (Pṛthvī) and should naturally be elevated and heavy; the Northeast represents Water (Jala) and Space (Ākāśa) and must remain low, open, and light. When the land slopes down to the Northeast, natural rain and solar energies circulate continuously.
methodology_explainer.solar_and_magnetic_science: Early morning sunbeams contain beneficial infrared and ultraviolet spectra that disinfect the ground. Sites that are open to the North and East capture the geomagnetic drift and morning sun, creating a thermally temperate and biochemically revitalizing microclimate.
methodology_explainer.marma_points: Irregular boundaries distort the primary diagonals (Vaṃśa-Sūtras). If a site has amputated corners or extended protuberances, the internal Vāstu Puruṣa becomes strained, creating localized zones of stagnant stagnation or hyper-acceleration.

Prakāśa-Samanvaya (Luminous Buoyancy): Utilizing bright upward-directed lighting along dark stairwells to visually and energetically lighten heavy concrete mass.
Pāda-Pīṭha Śodhana: Maintaining pristine cleanliness on treads and avoiding sharp metal nosing strips that concentrate cutting energy.
Yantra & Vāstu Pyramids: Embedding lead or brass pyramids beneath the lowest step of misplaced stairways to anchor runaway downward gravitational shear.
